title: Protocol to assemble metal-phenolic framework nanoparticles based on polyphenol-mediated biomimetic mineralization for wound healing in rats
protocol: Mix 40 mL of 1.02 mol/L Zn(OAc)₂·2H₂O and 40 mL of 0.73 mol/L 2-MIM stock solution under stirring with a magnetic bar.
Stop stirring after completely mixing the component solutions.
Let the mixture be at 25°C for 24 h to allow the ZIF-8 nanocrystal growth.
Collect the formed ZIF-8 nanoparticles by centrifuging (12,850 × g).
Wash three times with deionized water and methanol respectively.
Store the synthesized ZIF-8 NPs in methanol before using.
Transfer 6 mL of TA aqueous solution to a 20 mL synthetic flask containing a magnetic bar.
Add 1 mL of CaCl₂ solution to the flask.
Stir thoroughly.
Add 1 mL of Na₂O‧₃SiO₂ solution to the flask.
Stir thoroughly.
Centrifuge the methanol solution containing 8 mg of ZIF-8 at 12,850 × g.
Collect the ZIF-8 nanoparticles from the centrifuged solution.
Clean the collected ZIF-8 nanoparticles with DI water.
Disperse the cleaned ZIF-8 nanoparticles into 8 mL of MPS solution under ultrasound.
Stir the mixture for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge the mixture at 12,850 × g to collect MPFs nanoparticles (Zn-MPFs@CS).
Wash the collected MPFs nanoparticles with DI water three times.
Wash the collected MPFs nanoparticles with methanol three times.
Store Zn-MPFs@CS nanoparticles in methanol for further characterization and experiments.
Dissolve 0.027 g gelatin and 0.054 g chitosan hydrochloride in 1 mL of 1× PBS.
Stir the obtained gelatin-chitosan solution at 300 rpm for 36 h.
Dissolve 0.1 g transglutaminase in 500 μL of 1× PBS.
Stir the transglutaminase solution at 150 rpm for 24 h.
Filter the transglutaminase solution with a 0.22 μm filter.
Add 100 μL of sterile transglutaminase to the dissolved gelatin-chitosan solution containing 100 μg of Zn-MPFs@CS.
Incubate the mixture for 45 minutes at 37°C.
Anesthetize Sprague Dawley rats at 7 weeks old using isoflurane or another suitable anesthetic in an anesthesia box.
Move the anesthetized rats to a clean operating table.
Remove the back fur of the rats using a razor.
Disinfect the expected location of the wound with 75% ethanol.
Create a full-thickness skin wound model (diameter: ∼15 mm) on each rat’s back using sterilized scissors and forceps.
Take photos of the wounds for archiving purposes.
Spread the compound hydrogel over the wound surface using a syringe.
House each rat individually in a single cage after surgery.
Follow up on wound healing progress by recording the wound size regularly.
Take photos to document the wound healing process.
Collect regenerated wound tissue from each rat with sterilized scissors and forceps.
Cut the collected tissue into two strips.
Place the tissues in pre-filled 10% neutral buffered formalin container.
Fix the tissues for 48 hours.
Embed the fixed tissues with paraffin and Tissue-Tek O.C.T. compound, respectively.
Position the tissues onto a paraffin base mold for longitudinal sectioning of the tissue.
Place the base mold containing the tissues on a cold plate at -10°C to solidify the paraffin.
Place the pre-labeled cassette on top of the base mold containing the tissue.
Fill the mold with additional liquid paraffin.
Let the paraffin completely solidify before removing the paraffin block from the mold.
Trim excess paraffin from the sides of the cassette with the Para Trimmer.
Prewarm a 37°C water bath.
Mount the paraffin block on the microtome.
Cut 6 μm thin sections throughout the block to collect different layers of the tissues.
Pick up the sections using a small brush and transfer them gently into the water bath.
Dip a glass slide into the water bath and allow the tissue sections to adhere to the surface of the slide.
Exsiccate the slides in a slide box temporarily.
Place the slides in a 45°C incubator for 1 h.
Select the proper slide box for the classification, storage, and labeling of slides with tissues, which will be used for different staining and observation.
Place the glass slides with paraffin sections in staining racks.
Clear the paraffin from the samples in three changes of xylene for 10 min per change.
Stain the samples with different reagents following the H&E staining processor (Table 2).
Add a cover slip over the tissue on each slide.
View the slides using a microscope.
Place the glass slides with paraffin sections in staining racks.
Clear the paraffin from the samples in three changes of xylene for 10 min per change.
Stain the samples with different reagents following Masson’s Trichrome staining processor.
Incubate slides in 0.3% H2O2 on a gentle rocker and ensure slides are kept in a dark container as H2O2 is light-sensitive.
Embed tissues in OCT and freeze slides (10 μm) using a cryostat.
Stain the samples following the CD-31 immunofluorescent staining protocol.
View the slides using the DMi8 microscope.
